sents.t: Danny and Sarah have been looking for a house since the spring.
Their apartment, which has only two bedrooms, has become too small for a family of four.
Last Saturday, I went with them to an open house.
The house, which was built in 1950, is on a quiet street near Maple Park.
It has a big backyard with an old apple tree that Mia immediately wanted to climb.
The real estate agent, who wore a bright orange jacket, showed us every room.
“This is the kitchen that the owners remodeled last year,” she said.
Leo found a tiny room under the stairs and shouted, “This is the room where I want to sleep!”
“Remember, the house that we love isn’t always the house that we can afford,” Danny said quietly.
Even though he works at a bank, he was nervous about the mortgage, a loan that you pay back over fifteen or thirty years.
That evening, Danny and Sarah did the math at Rosa’s kitchen table.
With a down payment of twenty thousand dollars, which they had saved for five years, the monthly payment was possible.
They made an offer on Monday.
“Congratulations! The sellers have accepted your offer!”
“My son is a homeowner,” she said proudly.

comp.q: Why do Danny and Sarah need a new home?
o: They want to move to Chicago.
comp.fa: چرا دنی و سارا به خانه‌ی جدید نیاز دارند؟

o: to sleep in the room under the stairs

comp.q: What did Danny mean by “the house that we love isn’t always the house that we can afford”?
o: They might not have enough money for it.
comp.fa: منظور دنی از «the house that we love isn’t always the house that we can afford» چه بود؟

o: a loan to buy a home that you pay back over many years

comp.q: How long had they been saving for the down payment?
comp.fa: چند سال برای پیش‌پرداخت پول جمع کرده بودند؟
